_comment: Units of the questionnaire (which quantity kinds a property allows - including the choices for a concentration or a coverage - is stated in the ontology, cpo:valueHasQuantityKind), read by helpers/units.py. Moved out of the code on 25.09.2026: adding a unit is a data change, not a code change. Checked against the QUDT version named in ontology_library.jsonld by check_library_consistency.py. Keys starting with '_' are comments. CAUTION: every list here has answers in answers/*.txt behind it - keep the order and spelling of existing entries, only append.

units_by_quantity_kind._comment: Units offered per quantity kind. The unit hangs on EVERY value, not once on the series quantity: evidence and reference of the same quantity may come in different units, and a value added later would otherwise silently inherit another value's unit. Which quantity kind a property has is stated in the ontology (cpo:valueHasQuantityKind), not here.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_RotationalVelocity: Stirrer speeds (25.09.2026: moved from AngularVelocity, which QUDT does not give rpm for).
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_Entropy: Entropy of the whole phase (cpo:hasEntropy), not molar.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_Diameter: Device diameters (unit:M throughout the library) and particle sizes of dispersed phases - hence MicroM.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_geometry: The other device dimensions (cpo:hasHeight, hasLength, hasWidth, hasWallThickness and their inner/outer sub-properties). Added 25.09.2026, when the check against the ontology found that these kinds had no unit choice; the libraries give them in unit:M throughout.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_MolarMass: cpo:hasMolarMass of a chemical entity; the chemical entity library gives it in unit:GM-PER-MOL.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_ReactionRate: Project's own quantity kind, not a QUDT one (see cpo:ReactionRate in the ontology). Only one unit, asked all the same: a rate may be related to something else, e.g. the catalyst mass.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_concentrations: The concentration kinds WITH a unit among those the ontology allows for cpo:hasConcentration - the fractions there are in dimensionless_quantity_kinds.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_fields: Field strengths of the energy fields (see field_strength_quantity_kinds); Activity is radioactivity there, not chemical activity.
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_Acceleration: Field strength of a gravitational field (maintained by hand in the organization library).
units_by_quantity_kind._comment_rates: Change rates of a ramp (cpo:changeRate of a TransitionStep): the profile quantity per time, see change_rate_quantity_kinds.

change_rate_quantity_kinds._comment: Quantity kind of the change rate of a ramp step, per quantity kind of its profile. The rate is the profile quantity per time and has its own unit (K/min for a temperature ramp), not the unit of the profile. A profile kind that is missing here gets the general question for the kind of the rate. Each rate kind needs units in units_by_quantity_kind.

volume_unit_to_m3._comment: Conversion factors for the volume check (helpers/volume_checks.py: contents of a device against its inner volume). Same units as units_by_quantity_kind / quantitykind:Volume; the factors are checked against qudt:conversionMultiplier.

duration_units._comment: Units of a time:Duration (durations and start offsets of tasks, transfers, ...). A duration has no quantity kind - it is a time:Duration, not a ProcessVariable.

dimensionless_quantity_kinds._comment: Quantity kinds that have no unit by nature: every evidence/reference value of these kinds carries unit:UNITLESS without a question. ONLY on the value, never on the hlo:Actual. Deliberately separate from the kinds the ontology allows for cpo:hasConcentration, although the fractions overlap: those say WHAT a concentration can be expressed in (including MassConcentration and PartialPressure, both with a unit), this list which kinds have NO unit. Two questions, two lists.

fraction_quantity_kinds._comment: Real fractions (0..1) and how a percentage is accepted on INPUT: the word for the question text and the suffixes that fit the kind ('25 vol%' -> 0.25). The crate always holds the fraction, never the percentage (unit:PERCENT is deliberately not offered - two spellings of one quantity in one crate would have to be converted by every evaluation). A suffix of ANOTHER kind (wt% for a VolumeFraction) is refused; a bare '%' fits every kind. Not every dimensionless kind: quantitykind:Dimensionless (e.g. the partial order) may exceed 1.

field_strength_quantity_kinds._comment: Quantity kind of cpo:hasFieldStrength per field type, for the fields the generator creates itself (helpers/energy_fields.py); each must be one of the kinds the ontology allows for cpo:hasFieldStrength. The gravitational field is listed since 25.09.2026: the site's own field is maintained by hand, but an ambient field measured during a series is created by the generator (creation/environment_functions.py).

fixed_field_strength_units._comment: Unit written directly on a Fixed field strength (a field that exists only in a library, e.g. a radioactive substance: its activity in Bq).

accepted_dimension_matches._comment: Units QUDT does not list for the quantity kind (neither directly nor through skos:broader) although the dimension is the same. check_library_consistency.py reports every such pair unless it is accepted here, with the reason.

quantitykind:Entropy.unit:KiloJ-PER-K: QUDT attaches KiloJ-PER-K to EnergyPerTemperature only, J-PER-K to Entropy as well; same dimension vector, and the kJ variant is what data sheets give.
